document_summary: Part 1 of 5 of Los Angeles Municipal Code ch. XV, art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance), covering definitions, rent restrictions, registration, automatic annual adjustments (s 151.06) and the start of the security-deposit interest section (s 151.06.02), for Los Angeles, CA. | Part 2 of 5 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code, ch. XV art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance): the end of the §151.06 rent increase rules, security deposit interest (§151.06.02), surcharges and rent adjustments (§§151.06.1-151.08), and the start of §151.09 (Evictions), covering Los Angeles, CA. | Part 3 of 5 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code, ch. XV art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance), covering the end of LAMC 151.09 (eviction notice, relocation fees), sections 151.10 to 151.21 (remedies and administration) and the start of the Ellis Act sections 151.22 to 151.26, for Los Angeles, CA. | Part 4 of 5 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code, Chapter XV, Article 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance): Ellis Act re-rental rules, owner/family/manager occupancy evictions with relocation fees, buyout notification, COVID-era rent freeze, and the start of Article 2 (Tenant Habitability Program). Jurisdiction: City of Los Angeles, CA. | Part 5 of 5 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code ch. XV: the end of Art. 2 (tenant habitability and relocation for renovation work), Art. 3 (Habitability Enforcement Program), Art. 4 (property management training) and Art. 5 (Utility Maintenance Program), for Los Angeles, CA.

rules.title: LA RSO annual allowable rent increase (LAMC § 151.06 D)
rules.requirement: A landlord may raise rent annually by 90 percent of the CPI change (LA-Long Beach-Anaheim, 12-month averages ending September 30), rounded to the nearest whole number. The increase is at least 1 percent and never more than 4 percent, and only one such increase is allowed per 12 months.
rules.key_value: 90% of CPI change, minimum 1%, maximum 4% per year
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units under the RSO; housing in structures whose first Certificate of Occupancy was issued after October 1, 1978 is exempt. One-family dwellings are exempt unless two or more dwelling units are on the same parcel (duplexes and condominiums are not excepted). The Department publishes the allowable adjustment by May 30 each year; it applies to increases effective July 1 through June 30.
rules.exemptions: Exempt from the RSO: certificate of occupancy first issued after October 1, 1978; luxury housing certified by the Department; hotels/motels (until more than 30 days' occupancy); certain government-owned or regulated housing; affordable housing with a recorded 55-year regulatory agreement and an exemption certificate; and others. Housing Choice Voucher units are NOT exempt. No annual increase is allowed while a Franchise Tax Board noncompliance notice, a rent reduction or Rent Escrow Account Program placement, or a related criminal conviction remains uncorrected.
rules.interaction: Vacancy increases on re-rental are governed separately by § 151.06 C and the Costa-Hawkins Act; some vacancies limit re-rental to the prior lawful rent plus annual adjustments. The city formula operates alongside state law (Civ. Code § 1947.12).
rules.quoted_span:
The allowable annual rent adjustment shall be 90 percent of the percentage change rounded off to the nearest whole number as determined by the Department. If the allowable annual rent adjustment is less than one percent, a landlord
may increase the maximum or maximum adjusted rent by up to one percent. In no event, however, may an annual rent increase under this subsection exceed four
percent.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: two published effective dates for the new RSO formula (2026-02-02 per LAHD; 2026-01-24 per a landlord association). This capture shows only 'Amended by Ord. No. 188,795, Eff. 2/2/26'; the 2026-01-24 date is not found in this capture. A further amendment (Ord. No. 188,911, Eff. 4/20/26) is noted on the 'any annual rent increase that goes into effect' paragraph.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date taken from the code history note 'Amended by Ord. No. 188,795, Eff. 2/2/26' on subsection D. The 4% cap and 90%-of-CPI formula are from that amendment; the 1% floor is in the same text. Ord. 188,911 (Eff. 4/20/26) amended the paragraph requiring increases going into effect after the effective date to comply. Section 151.34 (temporary 4% setting) is not in this part.

rules.title: LA RSO payment of interest on security deposits (LAMC § 151.06.02)
rules.requirement: A landlord subject to Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 must pay annually interest on all security deposits held for at least one year for their tenants.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords subject to Civil Code § 1950.5 with RSO tenants; deposits held for at least one year.
rules.interaction: Local interest requirement layered on state security-deposit law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5); state law itself has no interest requirement.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord who is subject
to the provisions of Section 1950.5 of the California Civil Code shall pay annually interest on all security deposits held for at least one year for their
tenants as follows:
rules.extraction_notes: Document is truncated mid-section ('Beginning January 1, 2...'); the interest rate schedule is not in this capture, so key_value is null (rate likely in a later part). Effective date is the section's original 'Added by Ord. No. 166,368, Eff. 12/6/90'; subsections were later amended (Ord. 174,017 Eff. 7/16/01; Ord. 175,020 Eff. 2/1/03), which may have changed the rate, so the date of the current rate may differ.

rules.title: LA RSO additional-tenant rent increase (LAMC § 151.06 G)
rules.requirement: A landlord may raise the maximum rent or maximum adjusted rent by up to 10% for each additional tenant who joins the unit, subject to timely-notice conditions. This does not apply to a dependent added to an existing tenancy.
rules.key_value: Up to 10% per additional tenant (not for dependents)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the RSO. The increase is available only after the additional tenant has lived in the unit for 30 consecutive days.
rules.exemptions: Not available if the landlord knew of the additional tenant for more than 60 days and did not give notice of the increase. Not available for dependents added to an existing tenancy.
rules.interaction: A one-off increase on top of the annual allowable increase in § 151.06 D, which is not in this part of the document.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may increase the maximum rent or maximum adjusted rent by
   an amount not to exceed 10% for each additional tenant that joins the occupants
of the rental unit, except as follows:
rules.conflict_note: Open question: the new LA RSO formula has two published effective dates (2026-02-02 per LAHD, 2026-01-24 per a landlord association). The formula in § 151.06 D is not in this part. This part shows only Ord. 188,795 'Eff. 2/2/26' on the dependent exemption in G(a)(iii).
rules.extraction_notes: Supplementary to the headline annual cap in § 151.06 D, which is not in this part. G was amended by Ord. 181,744 (eff. 7/15/11); subdivision (iii) was amended by Ord. 188,795 (eff. 2/2/26). The 7/15/11 date is used for the 10% allowance.

rules.title: LA RSO individual rent adjustments and surcharges (LAMC §§ 151.06.1, 151.06.2, 151.07)
rules.requirement: Beyond the annual allowable increase, the Department may grant landlord-requested adjustments and temporary surcharges for capital improvements, rehabilitation, primary renovation and seismic work. Each is capped by formula, and surcharges are not counted as part of the maximum adjusted rent.
rules.key_value: Capital improvement surcharge: 1/60th of 50% of average per-unit cost, max $55/month, up to 6 years
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the RSO. Applications must be filed within 12 months after the work is completed.
rules.exemptions: Seismic Retrofit Work does not qualify as capital improvement, rehabilitation or primary renovation work. Exceptions apply where the unit is subject to a Franchise Tax Board noncompliance notice, a rent reduction or REAP notice, or a related criminal conviction.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside the annual cap in § 151.06 D, which is not in this part.
rules.quoted_span:
Except that, for any capital improvement work for which a rent increase
application is filed with the Department on or after October 1, 1989 the
landlord shall only be entitled to a temporary monthly rent increase of 1/60th
of fifty percent (50%) of the average per unit capital improvement cost for a
period not to exceed six (6) years.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: the new LA RSO formula has two published effective dates (2026-02-02 per LAHD, 2026-01-24 per a landlord association). The formula in § 151.06 D is not in this capture; this part shows only Ord. 188,795 'Eff. 2/2/26' deleting § 151.07 A.6.
rules.extraction_notes: Supplementary; fold into the annual cap record. Other ceilings: rehabilitation surcharge max $75/month or 10% of maximum adjusted rent, whichever is less, for up to 5 years; primary renovation increase max 10% of maximum adjusted rent, in two equal increments; seismic surcharge max $38/month over 120 months. Smoke detector surcharge: $0.50 (battery) or $3 (hardwired) per month. Water conservation penalty pass-through: 50% (75% for some mobilehome parks). Effective date null because the quoted rule gives only an application-date threshold (Oct. 1, 1989) and § 151.07 A.1 was last amended by Ord. 184,080 (eff. 2/19/16).

rules.title: LA payment of interest on security deposits (LAMC § 151.06.02)
rules.requirement: Landlords subject to Civ. Code § 1950.5 must pay tenants interest annually on security deposits held for at least one year. The landlord uses either the Rent Adjustment Commission's annual rate or the actual interest earned, and pays it as a payment or a rent credit.
rules.key_value: Annual interest on deposits held 1+ year at the RAC-set rate (or actual interest earned)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords subject to Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5, for deposits held at least one year.
rules.exemptions: Does not govern mobile home parks.
rules.interaction: Adds a local interest requirement on top of the state security-deposit statute, Civ. Code § 1950.5.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord who is subject to the provisions of Section 1950.5 of the California
Civil Code shall pay annually interest on all security deposits held for at least one year for their
tenants as follows:
rules.extraction_notes: Section added by Ord. 166,368 (eff. 12/6/90) with a 5% rate. The current rate-setting method (RAC rate or actual interest) dates from Ord. 175,020 (eff. 2/1/03), which is used as the effective date. Subsection B.4 was amended eff. 8/8/21 to have LAHD publish the rate. The current RAC rate is not stated in this document.

rules.title: LA RSO eviction only for enumerated grounds (LAMC § 151.09 A)
rules.requirement: A landlord may bring an action to recover possession of an RSO rental unit only on one of the listed grounds. These include non-payment above one month's HUD fair market rent, uncured lease violations, nuisance, illegal use, refusal to renew, and refusal of access. Others are owner or family move-in, primary renovation, demolition or withdrawal from the rental market, government orders, and others.
rules.key_value: Closed list of eviction grounds; for non-payment, arrears must exceed one month of HUD fair market rent for the LA metro area
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by LAMC ch. XV art. 1 (RSO). Coverage definitions are not in this part.
rules.interaction: Local just-cause rule for RSO units; its interaction with state just-cause law is not addressed in this part.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord may bring an action to recover possession of a rental unit
only upon one of the following grounds:
rules.extraction_notes: Section amended by Ord. 154,237 (Eff. 8/30/80, Oper. 9/1/80); operative date used. The non-payment threshold was added by Ord. 187,763 (eff. 3/27/23) and the occupancy-limit carve-out amended by Ord. 188,795 (eff. 2/2/26). The text is cut off in subsection C. Relocation-assistance provisions (e.g. § 151.30, Part 152) are not in this part. Owner move-in under A.8 must comply with § 151.30.

rules.title: LA RSO retaliatory eviction bar (LAMC § 151.09 B)
rules.requirement: A landlord whose dominant intent is retaliation for the tenant's exercise of RSO rights or complaint to an agency about tenantability may not recover possession, if the tenant is not in rent default.
rules.quoted_span:
If the dominant intent of the landlord in seeking to recover possession
of a rental unit is retaliation against the tenant for exercising the tenant’s
rights under this chapter or because of the tenant’s complaint to an
appropriate agency as to tenantability of a rental unit, and if the tenant is
not in default as to the payment of rent, then the landlord may not recover
possession of a rental unit in any action or proceeding or cause the tenant to
quit involuntarily.
rules.out_of_scope_reason: Anti-retaliation provision, excluded from the just-cause category by scope rules.

rules.title: LAMC § 151.09 G. relocation fees for no-fault evictions (RSO)
rules.requirement: When a tenancy is terminated on the no-fault grounds in Subdivisions 8., 10., 11., 12., 13. or 14. of § 151.09 A., the landlord must pay a relocation fee that depends on whether the tenant is qualified, how long they have lived in the unit, and their household income.
rules.key_value: $23,150 (qualified) / $11,000 (other) for under 3 years; $27,400 (qualified) / $14,400 (other) for 3+ years or household income at or below 80% AMI
rules.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance where termination rests on Subdivisions 8., 10., 11., 12., 13. or 14. of Subsection A. Where more than one fee applies, the landlord pays the highest.
rules.exemptions: Subsection G.4. exceptions include a replacement resident manager in the same unit and units made unsafe by fire, flood, earthquake or similar events beyond the owner's control.
rules.interaction: Other local, state or federal relocation benefits operate as a credit against this fee. Fees adjust annually from July 1, 2026 under § 151.06 D., based on 100% of the change and rounded to the nearest $50.
rules.quoted_span: Except for relocation fees owed pursuant to the provisions of Subsection E. of Section 151.30 of this Code, if the termination of tenancy is based on the grounds set forth in Subdivisions 8., 10., 11., 12., 13. or 14. of Subsection A. of this section, then the landlord shall pay a relocation fee of: $23,150 to qualified tenants and a $11,000 fee to all other tenants who have lived in their rental unit for fewer than three years; $27,400 to qualified tenants and a $14,400 fee to all other tenants who have lived in their rental unit for three years or longer;
rules.extraction_notes: Amounts as amended by Ord. No. 188,795, Eff. 2/2/26. The full grounds list (§ 151.09 A.) is in another part of the document. The sentence is longer than 800 characters, so the quote stops before the income-based clause. Landlords also pay the City a service-provider fee ($971 per qualified-tenant unit, $604 per other unit, plus $83 admin) for grounds 8., 10., 11. and 12. The 2/2/26 date is for this relocation amendment, not the separate RSO rent formula open question.

rules.title: LAMC § 151.09 B. anti-retaliation
rules.requirement: A landlord may not recover possession or force a tenant out where the dominant intent is retaliation for the tenant exercising RSO rights or complaining to an agency about tenantability, provided the tenant is not in rent default.
rules.quoted_span: If the dominant intent of the landlord in seeking to recover possession of a rental unit is retaliation against the tenant for exercising the tenant’s rights under this chapter or because of the tenant’s complaint to an appropriate agency as to tenantability of a rental unit, and if the tenant is not in default as to the payment of rent, then the landlord may not recover possession of a rental unit in any action or proceeding or cause the tenant to quit involuntarily.
rules.out_of_scope_reason: Anti-retaliation provision, excluded from just-cause scope.
rules.extraction_notes: Last amended by Ord. No. 161,865, Eff. 1/19/87; the date is an amendment, not a first-effective date, so effective_date is left null.

rules.title: LAMC § 151.23 Ellis Act withdrawal notice (120 days / one year)
rules.requirement: A landlord withdrawing or demolishing RSO units must file a Notice of Intent to Withdraw with the Department, and the withdrawal date must be at least 120 days after delivery. Qualifying tenants who are 62 or older or disabled and have lived in the unit at least one year get an extension to one year.
rules.key_value: At least 120 days' notice; one year for qualifying seniors/disabled tenants
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, occupied or vacant. Extension requires the tenant to be at least 62 or disabled, to have lived there at least one year, and to give written notice within 60 days.
rules.exemptions: Residential hotels as defined in Health & Safety Code § 50519 and LAMC § 47.70 et seq. (§ 151.22).
rules.interaction: Implements California Ellis Act (Gov. Code § 7060 et seq.). Relocation fees under § 151.09 G. also apply to ground 10.
rules.quoted_span: The date on which the rental units are to be withdrawn from rental housing use shall be at least 120 days from the date of the delivery to the Department in person or by first-class mail of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw.
rules.extraction_notes: Section added by Ord. No. 177,901, Eff. 9/29/06; amended by Ord. No. 184,873, Eff. 6/4/17 (subsection B. wording and annual reports), with the 120-day requirement unchanged. Supplementary to the § 151.09 A. just-cause grounds list found in another part of the source.

rules.title: LAMC § 151.30 – Evictions for owner, family, or resident manager occupancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict an RSO tenant for owner, relative or resident-manager occupancy only if the landlord meets the ownership thresholds and good-faith two-year occupancy rules, no comparable unit is vacant, and no protected tenant is in the unit. Relocation fees under § 151.09 G apply, with fixed fees for qualifying small landlords.
rules.key_value: Ownership of at least 25% (para. a) or 50% (para. b); occupancy within 3 months for 2 consecutive years; small-landlord relocation fee $21,250 (qualified tenants) / $10,550 (others), adjusted annually from July 1, 2026
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to terminations under § 151.09 A.8. Protected tenants: resident 10+ years and aged 62+ or disabled, or terminally ill. Small-landlord fee exception requires a building of four or fewer units, no fee paid in the previous three years, and no more than four units plus one single-family home owned in the City.
rules.exemptions: Resident-manager replacement allowed where the building has an existing resident manager. Protected tenants (10+ year residents aged 62+ or disabled; terminally ill) cannot be evicted under this ground. Small-landlord relocation-fee exception as described in coverage_conditions.
rules.interaction: Supplements the main just-cause grounds and the relocation schedule in LAMC § 151.09 (found in another part of the document). State Tenant Protection Act rules (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2) are not addressed in this document.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord may recover possession of a rental unit pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph a of Subdivision 8. of Subsection A. of Section 151.09 only if the landlord is a natural person who possesses legal title to at least 25 percent of the property containing the rental unit, or is a beneficiary with an interest of at least 25 percent in a trust that owns the property.
rules.extraction_notes: Section added by Ord. No. 180,747, Eff. 8/1/09. Subsection E (relocation fee amounts) amended by Ord. No. 188,795, Eff. 2/2/26; that date is used because it changed the fee values. Ord. 188,795 is the same ordinance tied to the LA RSO formula date dispute (2026-02-02 per LAHD vs 2026-01-24 per landlord association); this part states 2/2/26 for § 151.30 E only. The headline just-cause grounds and the general relocation schedule are in § 151.09, which is in another part.  Landlords must also file post-termination occupancy statements and offer re-rental to the displaced tenant within two years.  Fee adjustment starts the year beginning July 1, 2026.  Bad-faith recovery is penalised at three times actual damages.

rules.title: LAMC § 151.26 – Rent on re-offer after Ellis Act withdrawal
rules.requirement: If a unit withdrawn from the rental market under the Ellis Act is re-offered within five years of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or of the withdrawal, it must be rented at the lawful rent in effect when the notice was filed, plus annual adjustments under § 151.06.
rules.key_value: Rent reset to the rent in effect when the Notice of Intent to Withdraw was filed, plus § 151.06 annual adjustments, for five years
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units that were the subject of a Notice of Intent to Withdraw under § 151.23 A and are re-offered for rent or lease within five years of the notice filing or of the withdrawal.
rules.exemptions: Replacement units built after demolition are governed by § 151.28, which allows the owner to set the initial rent but applies the RSO, with exemptions for replacement affordable units and certain owner-occupants.
rules.interaction: Prevails over any conflicting provision of law that lets the landlord set the rent on initial hiring of a rental unit. The City may apply the constraints to a successor in interest by recording a notice (Cal. Gov. Code § 7060.3).
rules.quoted_span: If a rental unit that was removed from rental housing use pursuant to the provisions of Section 151.23 is offered for rent or lease during either: 1. the five-year period after the Notice of Intent to Withdraw the accommodations is filed with the Department pursuant to Section 151.23, whether or not the Notice of Intent is rescinded or the withdrawal of the accommodations is completed pursuant to the Notice of Intent; or 2. the five-year period after the accommodations are withdrawn; then the accommodations shall be offered and rented or leased at the lawful rent in effect at the time any Notice of Intent to Withdraw the accommodations was filed with the Department, plus annual adjustments available under Section 151.06 of this article.
rules.extraction_notes: Section added by Ord. No. 177,901, Eff. 9/29/06; subsections C and D added by Ord. No. 184,873, Eff. 6/4/17. This is a special-case rent rule, not the general annual RSO cap, which is in § 151.06 (another part of the document). The COVID-era freeze (§ 151.32) and the temporary 4% setting (§ 151.34, repealed 6/30/24) were not extracted because they have lapsed.

rules.title: UMP anti-retaliation bar on recovery of possession (LAMC § 155.05 C)
rules.requirement: A landlord whose dominant intent in seeking possession is retaliation against a tenant for exercising Utility Maintenance Program rights may not recover possession or force the tenant out, if the tenant is not in default on rent (including payments into UMP).
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in master-metered buildings placed into the Utility Maintenance Program (UMP).
rules.quoted_span: If the dominant intent of the landlord(s) in seeking to recover possession of a residential unit is retaliation against the tenant for exercising their rights under this Article, and if the tenant is not in default as to the payment of rent, including payments into UMP, then the landlord(s) may not recover possession of a residential unit in any action or proceeding or cause the tenant to quit involuntarily.
rules.out_of_scope_reason: Anti-retaliation provision, not a limit on grounds for eviction or non-renewal; logged, not published.
rules.extraction_notes: Section amended by Ord. No. 181,643, Eff. 5/31/11, but that date is for the amendment of the section as a whole, so effective_date is left null. The rest of this part (§§ 152.05 D-152.08, Arts. 3-5) covers temporary relocation during renovation, habitability enforcement, training and utility escrow. None of that sets a just-cause ground or a rent cap. The § 151.09 text named in the manifest is not in this part.
